title: docs(qa): re-point the eight accept-set checklist anchors at their enclosing declarations
body:
Fixes #18101
Clause-②: no
Ruling-ref: 5748968793

## What this does

The shared symbol-anchor resolver refuses eight platform-checklist anchors that name real sites: six are object-literal keys written INLINE in config, seed, datasource and action literals, and two are data identifiers (`sys_user`, `sys_invitation`) that appear only as the HEAD of dotted action names. Under the ruling on the card (letter C), the shared core in `scripts/symbol-anchors.mjs` is **not** widened, and no citation is dropped to a bare one. Each anchor now points at the nearest enclosing declaration the resolver does read, so every pointer stays checkable. The eight `accept-set` rows leave `SHARED_RESOLVER_RESIDUAL` by repair.

`scripts/symbol-anchors.mjs` is untouched; `git diff 05be35259 -- scripts/symbol-anchors.mjs` is empty.

## The eight rows

How I picked each one: the first segment is always the top-level declaration that encloses the literal. I add a member segment only when the cited sentence names that member itself (the `admin` / `organization` feature entries, the `parent` field). The config file is the one exception. Its default export is an anonymous `defineStack(...)` call, so its nearest enclosing declaration that resolves is the `plugins` key. Each re-pointed value also gets a `re-pointed #18101: ...` note saying why, following the trace the `bad-citation` drain cuts used.

| area file | old anchor | new anchor | why this declaration encloses the cited site |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dashboards.json` | `examples/app-showcase/src/data/seed/index.ts#signed_on` | `...#accounts` | `signed_on` is set inline in each account seed row. `const accounts = defineSeed(Account, ...)` declares those rows. |
| `dashboards.json` | `examples/app-showcase/src/data/seed/index.ts#sales_region` | `...#accounts` | Same rows: `sales_region` and `signed_on` are both inline keys of the records in the `accounts` seed constant. |
| `identity-auth.json` | `packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts#sys_invitation` | `...#PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES.organization` | The three `sys_invitation.actions.*` tokens all sit in `PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES.organization.gatedInputs`. The sentence is about the organization feature. |
| `identity-auth.json` | `packages/spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts#sys_user` | `...#PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES.admin` | The `sys_user` lifecycle action tokens (create / ban / unban / unlock / set password / impersonate) sit in `PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES.admin.gatedInputs`. The sentence is about the admin flag. |
| `integration-system.json` | `examples/app-showcase/objectstack.config.ts#declarativeStdio` | `...#plugins` | `declarativeStdio` is inline in `new ConnectorMcpPlugin({ ... })`, an element of the `plugins:` array. The config is an anonymous `export default defineStack(...)`, and `defineStack` / `ConnectorMcpPlugin` are imports, which do not resolve. `plugins` is the nearest enclosing key the resolver reads. |
| `integration-system.json` | `examples/app-showcase/src/system/datasources/showcase-external.datasource.ts#onMismatch` | `...#ShowcaseExternalDatasource` | `onMismatch` is inline in `external.validation`. `export const ShowcaseExternalDatasource = defineDatasource(...)` is the datasource constant that holds it, and the file's only declaration. |
| `records-forms.json` | `examples/app-showcase/src/ui/actions/index.ts#maxSize` | `...#ActionParamGalleryAction` | Both `maxSize` sites (the `p_cover` and `p_attachments` params) are inline in the `params` of `export const ActionParamGalleryAction`. No other action in the file sets `maxSize`. |
| `records-forms.json` | `examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/business-unit.object.ts#allowCreate` | `...#BusinessUnit.parent` | `allowCreate: true` is inline in the options of the `parent: Field.lookup(...)` field of `export const BusinessUnit`. The sentence is "parent allowCreate:true". |

I probed every new anchor through `symbolSegmentResolution` before editing (every segment `declaration`, none `literal`), then confirmed it with the gate run below.

## The ceiling: 18 → 10

At `origin/main` `05be35259` the ceiling is already 18, not the 55 the ruling quotes; the `bad-citation` drain lowered it after the ruling was written. The ledger's own drain contract says: "the citation is re-pointed at what the cited file actually declares, the row goes, and the ceiling below comes down by the same number in the same edit. ⛔ Never by raising the ceiling". So removing 8 rows takes `SHARED_RESOLVER_RESIDUAL_CEILING` from 18 to 10, and rows == ceiling again. That matches the ruling's intent (the ledger is shrink-only). Only the number 55 has moved since then.

I also updated the ledger prose that this change made false:
- the second- and third-slice notes said these files "still carry" their `accept-set` rows;
- the `accept-set` verdict description said the rows were "a different card, against the shared core".

The `accept-set` verdict stays in the closed two-verdict vocabulary with **0 rows**. The shape it names still exists; the ruling only decided how such a row is repaired. I added a short drain paragraph that records the ruling.

## Verification (at `9919256b81`)

`pnpm check:platform-checklist` is red on `main` because of ONE unrelated row: `areas/identity-auth.json` → `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts#twoFactor`, already filed as #20464. That row is not touched here and stays red. The proof for this PR is that this one problem stays, no new one appears, and the eight residual rows are gone.

| reading | before (`05be35259`) | after (`9919256b81`) |
|---|---|---|
| `pnpm check:platform-checklist` | exit 1, `1 problem(s)`: the #20464 `twoFactor` row | exit 1, `1 problem(s)`: the same #20464 `twoFactor` row, nothing else |
| `--anchor-census` resolved | 628/647 | 636/647 |
| on the named residual | 18 | 10 |
| per-file floor population (resolved + residual) | dashboards 22 · identity-auth 82 · integration-system 57 · records-forms 84 | identical (census JSON byte-equal), so no floor moves and none was touched |
| `node scripts/check-platform-checklist.mjs --self-test` | 221 assertions, exit 0 | 221 assertions, exit 0 |

Intermediate reading: I ran the gate with the anchors already re-pointed and the ledger not yet edited. It printed exactly 8 `STALE RESIDUAL ROW` reds, one per row, plus the #20464 row, and no `ABSENT SYMBOL` for any new anchor. That shows the gate really reads the eight re-pointed citations, and that each one resolves.

One-shot mutation (run from the committed state, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, restore verified): I changed the re-pointed `#accounts` in `areas/dashboards.json` to `#accountz`. The gate printed `ABSENT SYMBOL — examples/app-showcase/src/data/seed/index.ts#accountz` and `SYMBOL ANCHORS LOST — 21 anchor(s) resolve here but the floor is 22`, alongside the #20464 row. After the run the file blob equals HEAD (`85e8f6f4a702`) and `git diff HEAD` is empty. So a re-pointed anchor is still checked both ways: by the resolver, and by the per-file floor. No test file was added for this.

Every gate `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands` derives for this diff (32 commands, change set from merge base `05be35259`), run at `9919256b81`. `--ran` reconciles them as `32 derived, 32 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN` (every line exit-coded):

- **exit 0 (30 commands):** `check-ci-filter-parity`, `check-closing-keyword-parity` (+ `--self-test`), `check-comment-mask-corpus`, `check-declaration-mirrors` (+ `--self-test`), `check-scripts-symbol-anchors` (+ `--self-test`; this corpus reads the new comment prose in the gate script), `check-self-test-wired` (+ `--self-test`), `check-self-test-workflow-commands` (+ `--self-test`), `check-whole-set-label-write` (+ `--self-test`), `pm/bare-root-worklist --self-test`, and `pnpm check:` `agent-test-spelling` · `bash32-floor` · `cli-command-ids` · `cross-package-test-inputs` · `doc-authoring` · `driver-memory-census` · `entry-guard` · `gitlink-declared` · `nul-bytes` · `parse-guard` · `pnpm-filter-targets` · `ratchet-remedy-authority` · `refd-timer-probe` · `watch-hint-literal`.
- **exit 0, re-run (2 commands):**
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint run check:doc-formula-expressions` first exited 3 with PREREQUISITE NOT MET: `@objectstack/formula` and `@objectstack/lint` had no `dist/`, so nothing was measured. I built both under the verify lock and re-ran it: exit 0.
  - `pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates`: my batch runner's time cap killed the first attempt. I ran it alone to completion: exit 0, `dispatch-gates self-test: 1976 cases pass`, battery 912.6 s on this shared box.
- **exit 1 (1 command):** `pnpm check:platform-checklist`, on the one #20464 row only, as shown above.

## Changeset

None needed. `docs/qa/**` and the root `scripts/` directory sit outside every package directory, and the root package is `private`. Across 81 tracked `package.json` files, no non-private package's `files[]` names either path. ⇒ `skip-changeset`.

## Acceptance notes

- The `shape` legend in the ledger header still gives the per-shape counts from when the binding was made ("string-substring … 12 rows", "import-only … 6 rows", …). The 10 live rows are 5 / 3 / 2. These are old dated readings and not a defect. I did not touch them here because they are outside this card's 8 rows. Nobody is carrying this.
- Self-test `D4` still reads "the `accept-set` rows are the minority and are named as a DIFFERENT card". It holds numerically (zero `accept-set` rows against ten `bad-citation` rows), but the label is out of date after the ruling. I kept the change to the surface the ruling names, so the label is not edited here.
